subject.title: [Bug]: Local `openclaw agent` drops owner-only tools without `--model`

question: What verified trust fact should grant owner identity to configured local `openclaw agent` calls without elevating remote or explicit non-owner callers?
rationale: The behavioral defect is established, but prior merged changes intentionally preserve ordinary least privilege and non-owner loopback filtering, so maintainers must choose the permanent privilege-elevation boundary.

options.title: Use resolved local target
options.body: Grant backend/admin identity only when dispatch resolution selects the configured local loopback Gateway, leaving remote mode and explicit URL overrides non-admin.

options.title: Use server-verified transport
options.body: Keep the CLI identity unchanged and elevate only after the Gateway verifies authenticated local transport context.

options.title: Require explicit owner mode
options.body: Retain ordinary least privilege and introduce a separate explicit owner invocation for privileged local turns.

recommendation.title: Use resolved local target
recommendation.body: Grant backend/admin identity only when dispatch resolution selects the configured local loopback Gateway, leaving remote mode and explicit URL overrides non-admin.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest recent owner of the CLI Gateway dispatch path, landed the existing authorization split, and reported the intended local-versus-remote behavior.
